results.key_finding: Standard treatment for cerebral toxoplasmosis is pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin for 6 weeks (acute phase) followed by maintenance therapy. For patients with sulfonamide allergy, pyrimethamine + clindamycin + leucovorin is an established alternative first-line regimen. Imaging response at 2 weeks is used to confirm diagnosis; tissue biopsy is considered if no radiological improvement. Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) is a recognized risk with antiretroviral therapy optimization in active opportunistic infection.

patient.history_present_illness: A 48-year-old Black male construction foreman was brought to the emergency department by EMS after a witnessed fall at a construction worksite. His coworkers reported he had a brief tonic-clonic seizure lasting about 90 seconds while walking, fell to the ground, and struck the right side of his head on concrete. He was wearing no helmet (office area of the site). After the seizure stopped, he did not regain normal consciousness. EMS found him confused, agitated, GCS 10, with a visible right temporal laceration and scalp hematoma. He arrived 35 minutes after the fall. He has no prior history of seizures. Coworkers report he was acting normally at work today. No alcohol or drug use at the worksite per coworkers. He has a history of HIV infection, diagnosed 4 years ago, on antiretroviral therapy. His most recent CD4 count was 382 cells/mm3 (6 weeks ago), and his viral load was undetectable (<20 copies/mL). He takes bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (Biktarvy) daily. He also takes atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia. He has no known history of CNS opportunistic infections. His wife reports he was entirely well this morning with no complaints. No prior head trauma. Social history: former moderate drinker (quit 1 year ago), non-smoker, no illicit drugs.
